title: the gates stop repeating CI: the local full-check gate is removed, fail-first runs only the touched suites, and gate runs are serialized
acceptance: Gate 3 is a full local run of the project check. It duplicates the required GitHub check, and on 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-26 it held CI-green heads by overrunning its 600s budget whenever run-mode reviewers or other gates ran ci.sh at the same time (1565s on T-104, and again on T-068, T-086, T-112 and T-054). The captain approved removing it (2026-09-26). This item is split out of T-107. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-114.json, is committed on this branch.

Gate 3 is removed. The evidence it gave is the required GitHub check on the same head, which gate 6 already reads. The remaining gates keep their meaning. Every place that counts or numbers the gates is updated consistently: bin/fm-gate.sh (its header, the exit codes and the say() lines), bin/fm-run.sh, bin/fm.sh, bin/fm-review.sh, the board, the skills (firstmate, reviewer, worker), README.md and design/design.md. So nothing still says 'seven gates' or refers to gate 3 as the local check. Whether the gates are renumbered or gate 3 is left as a retired number is the worker's call, stated and applied everywhere, including the board and the tests that match gate lines.

Gate 5 (reverting the implementation turns tests red) re-runs only the test suites the diff touches, or that exercise a file the diff changes where that is determinable, instead of the whole project check. When no suite can be determined, it falls back to the whole check and says so.
Gate runs on one machine are serialized by a lock, so two gate runs never overlap.

Evidence is the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Tests written to fail first in tests/gate.test.sh cover: no gate runs the project check in full; gate 5 runs only the touched suites and turns red when the implementation is reverted; two concurrent fm-gate.sh runs serialize; and the gate lines and numbers match everything that reads them (board, diagram and selfupdate suites). The worker does not run the suite itself.
